4. Do not use the /tmp folder in the root of the machine since it will be outside of your permitted areas to work.
# Versioning Policy — SemVer Tag Governance

> [!CAUTION]
> **FLASH GATE — read this before every firmware upload.**
>
> Building for compilation testing is fine without tagging.
> But **before flashing to hardware**, if the firmware includes **any** new
> functionality since the last tag:
> 1. Check the current highest tag: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`
> 2. Increment the dev PRE_NUM: `git tag v0.X.Y-dev.(N+1) && git push origin v0.X.Y-dev.(N+1)`
> 3. Rebuild (so `inject_version.py` picks up the new tag at compile time)
> 4. **Then** flash.
>
> This is **autonomous** — `dev` tags do not require user approval.
> Skip this step **only** if the firmware contains NO new functionality.
>
> **The sequence is: Tag → Build → Flash. Never flash an untagged build.**

### Pre-flash checklist

Before calling `upload_firmware`, `agent_flash_monitor_verify`, or any
esptool/OTA upload command, stop and verify:

- [ ] Does this firmware contain new functionality since the last `dev` tag?
- [ ] If yes: have I tagged, pushed, **and rebuilt** so the version is baked in?
- [ ] `curl /api/system` after boot — does `firmware_version` match the new tag?

---

## Quick Reference

| Tag format              | Channel  | Agent can tag? | Requires user? |
|-------------------------|----------|---------------|----------------|
| `v0.X.Y-dev.N`         | Dev      | ✅ Yes         | No             |
| `v0.X.Y-beta.N`        | Beta     | ❌ No          | Yes            |
| `v0.X.Y`               | Stable   | ❌ No          | Yes            |

| Action                        | Agent autonomy | Requires user approval |
|-------------------------------|---------------|------------------------|
| Create `dev` tag              | ✅ Yes         | No                     |
| Create `beta` / `stable` tag  | ❌ No          | Yes                    |
| Increment `PATCH`/`MINOR`/`MAJOR` | ❌ No     | Yes                    |
| Run `deploy_release.py` (any) | ❌ No*          | Yes (User runs CLI)    |

* **Agents MUST NEVER execute `deploy_release.py` directly.** The private key requires an interactive passphrase, which causes background agent tasks to hang indefinitely on `openssl`. Always output the exact CLI command and ask the user to run it in their terminal.

## Mechanical Enforcement

This rule is **enforced by a `PreToolUse` lifecycle hook** (`.agents/hooks.json`
→ `flash-tag-gate`). The hook runs before every `upload_firmware` and
`agent_flash_monitor_verify` MCP call and will **hard-deny** the flash if HEAD
has untagged commits. The denial message includes the exact tag command to run.

The agent does not need to remember this checklist — the runtime will block it.
The rule text above remains as educational context explaining *why* tagging
matters and the conventions for tag formats.

## Full Policy Reference

For tag anatomy, three-tier release model, decision tree, and tag hygiene
rules see: [`docs/developer/versioning-policy.md`](../../docs/developer/versioning-policy.md)
# 04-MCP Tooling Priority

For this project (esp32-app-foundation), we use the `platformio` MCP server for all PlatformIO-related tasks. 

**Rule:**
When compiling, building, cleaning, uploading firmware/filesystem, or performing other PlatformIO operations, you **MUST** prioritize using the `platformio` MCP tools (e.g., `build_project`, `clean_project`, `upload_firmware`, `run_tests`) over running direct `pio` CLI commands in the terminal.

**Why:** 
This ensures the MCP server correctly manages the project state, locks, and environment across different agents. If you are delegating tasks to worker agents, you must explicitly instruct them to use these MCP tools rather than raw CLI commands.

## Mechanical Enforcement

This rule is **enforced by a `PreToolUse` lifecycle hook** (`.agents/hooks.json`
→ `pio-cli-gate`). The hook intercepts every `run_command` call and checks
whether the command invokes `pio`, `platformio`, `esptool`, or `esptool.py`
directly.

If a direct CLI invocation is detected, the hook issues a **`force_ask`**
decision — the user must explicitly approve each individual invocation. The
"Always Allow" cache is deliberately bypassed so that debugging permissions
are never sticky.

**For agents:** Do not attempt to use `pio` or `esptool` directly. Use the
MCP tools. If the hook blocks you, it means you should be using
`build_project`, `upload_firmware`, etc. instead.

## Summary

`Application::setAppName()` correctly propagates to the **web portal title** and **boot screen**, but three other user-facing surfaces use independent, disconnected naming mechanisms. A consumer calling `app.setAppName("Weather Station")` sees that name in the portal but sees `"ESP32"` in BLE scans, `"esp32-foundation"` as the WiFi AP SSID, and must manually wire Home Assistant.

## Audit — Current State

| Surface | Source | Default | Uses `getAppName()`? |
|---------|--------|---------|---------------------|
| **Web portal title** | `APP_TITLE` → `setAppName()` override | `"ESP32 App Foundation"` | ✅ Yes |
| **Boot screen** | `BootBoard::setAppTitle()` via `Application::begin()` | `"ESP32 App Foundation"` | ✅ Yes |
| **WiFi AP SSID** | `WifiManager::setDefaultHostname()` — separate call in `main.cpp` | `"esp32-foundation"` | ❌ No |
| **WiFi STA hostname** | Same `_currentHostname` | `"esp32-foundation"` | ❌ No |
| **BLE advertised name** | `BLEConfig::advertisedName` from persisted config JSON | `"ESP32"` | ❌ No |
| **Home Assistant** | `haModule.setAppName(app.getAppName())` — manual wiring | `"ESP32 Device (XX:XX)"` | ⚠️ Manual |
| **BLE DIS** | Does not exist yet | — | ❌ N/A |
| **mDNS** | Not audited | — | Unknown |

### The Problem in Practice

Every consumer `main.cpp` currently needs three separate setter calls, and BLE is not wired at all:

```cpp
app.setAppName("Weather Station");                          // portal + boot
app.getWifiManager().setDefaultHostname("WeatherStation");  // WiFi AP — separate!
haModule.setAppName(app.getAppName());                      // HA — manual!
// BLE: user must change config JSON or it stays "ESP32"
```

### Key Files

- `modules/Application/Application.hpp` — `setAppName()` / `getAppName()` (lines 168-171)
- `modules/Application/Application.cpp` — propagates to boot reporter (line 95) and web server (line 263)
- `modules/WifiManager/WifiManager.cpp` — `setDefaultHostname()` (line 395), AP SSID uses `_currentHostname` (line 279)
- `modules/BLEManager/BLEManager.hpp` — `advertisedName = "ESP32"` (line 103)
- `modules/WebServer/WebServerManager.hpp` — `APP_TITLE` fallback (lines 52-53)
- `modules/U8G2Display/boards/BootBoard.hpp` — `APP_TITLE` fallback (lines 32-33)
- `modules/HomeAssistant/HomeAssistantModule.cpp` — `_appName` (line 193)
- `src/main.cpp` — three separate setter calls (lines 114, 130)

## Proposed Solution

### Option A: Centralised Identity in `Application` (Recommended)

`Application` becomes the single source of truth for device identity. All modules pull from it rather than maintaining independent name fields.

1. **`Application::setAppName(const char* name)`** already exists. Extend `Application::begin()` to propagate the app name to all registered modules:

```cpp
// In Application::begin(), after module registration:
_wifiManager.setDefaultHostname(sanitiseHostname(getAppName()));

if (_bleManager) {
    _bleManager->setDefaultAdvertisedName(getAppName());
}

// HA auto-wires in Application::begin() already — just ensure it uses getAppName()
```

2. **Add `sanitiseHostname()`** — converts app name to a valid hostname (lowercase, hyphens, max 32 chars). `"Weather Station"` → `"weather-station"`.

3. **`BLEManager::setDefaultAdvertisedName()`** — sets the factory default for `advertisedName` config field (like `WifiManager::setDefaultHostname()` pattern). Persisted user config still overrides it.

4. **Add firmware version to identity** — `Application` should expose `getVersion()` returning the build-time `FIRMWARE_VERSION` string, usable by DIS, `/api/system/info`, OTA headers, and HA.

### Option B: Identity Struct

Create a `DeviceIdentity` struct populated once and passed to all modules:

```cpp
struct DeviceIdentity {
    const char* appName;
    const char* version;
    const char* manufacturer;
    const char* boardModel;
    uint64_t    chipId;
};
```

More formal but heavier change. Could be a v2 evolution of Option A.

### Migration Impact

- **Framework code**: Moderate — wire propagation in `Application::begin()`, add sanitiser, add `BLEManager::setDefaultAdvertisedName()`.
- **Consumer code**: Simplifies — one `setAppName()` call replaces three. Existing multi-call patterns still work.
- **Breaking changes**: None. All existing setter APIs remain. The change adds automatic defaults that consumers can still override.

## Related

- BLE DIS implementation (forthcoming — will consume the same identity)
- RFC #230: OTA module unloading
- `docs/developer/bluetooth.md` § Memory & DRAM Budget

6: # Harness Adapter — Antigravity
7: 
8: You are running under **Antigravity** (harness-hosted runtime — the CLI / chat interface, not a programmatic SDK agent). You confirmed this by self-inspection (Core Directive 6): your sub-agent spawn tool is `invoke_subagent`. This adapter governs how you spawn and right-size workers here.

11: > This adapter applies to the **harness-hosted runtime** only. If you are building a programmatic agent via the Google Antigravity Python SDK, the `LocalAgentConfig` does expose a `model` field per agent — in that context, refer to the model-selection guidance in the SDK documentation instead.
12: 
13: ## Spawn Mechanics
14: 
15: Spawn workers using the **`invoke_subagent`** tool with `TypeName: "self"` — this inherits the full harness configuration including tools, skills, and system prompt, making it the correct type for capable execution workers.
16: 
17: Key parameters to set on every Work Order spawn:
18: 
19: | Parameter | Value | Rationale |
20: |---|---|---|
21: | `TypeName` | `"self"` | Inherits full harness config; gives the worker all necessary tools. |
22: | `Role` | `"Execution Worker"` | Human-readable identity for the worker in the subagent list. |
23: | `Prompt` | bridge prompt from Step 4 | The full WORKORDER bridge prompt. |
24: | `Model` | See complexity mapping below | **Always set explicitly** — maps from the WORKORDER's `complexity` field. |
25: | `Workspace` | See decision table below | **Do not default to `"branch"` — read the decision table.** |
26: 
27: ### `Workspace` Mode Decision
28: 
29: > [!CAUTION]
30: > **`"branch"` creates an isolated worktree at a path outside the user's permitted
31: > directory** (e.g. inside `~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/.../worktrees/`). The subagent
32: > will have **no permissions** for that path and will prompt the user for approval on
33: > every single file read or write. This defeats the purpose of autonomous execution.
34: 
35: | Scenario | Use | Rationale |
36: |---|---|---|
37: | **Single serialised worker** (most PRs — one WO at a time) | **`"inherit"`** | Worker operates in the same directory as the PA, which is already permitted. The branch is already checked out before spawning. No permission prompts. |
38: | **Truly parallel workers** on different branches simultaneously | **`"branch"`** | Gives each worker its own isolated worktree so they cannot clobber each other's staged changes. Only viable when the user has explicitly granted permissions to the worktree root path, or is prepared to approve access on first spawn. |
39: 
40: **The standard PA workflow (one WO at a time, branch pre-checked-out) always uses `"inherit"`.**
41: Use `"branch"` only when you have confirmed the user's permission grants cover the worktree path,
42: or when the user has explicitly requested parallel execution and accepted the permission prompts.
43: 
44: ### Async / Auto-Wake Behaviour
45: 
46: `invoke_subagent` is **inherently asynchronous**. After spawning:
47: 1. Inform the user the worker is running in the background.
48: 2. **Drop control immediately** — do not poll or loop.
49: 3. The system will **automatically wake you** when the worker sends a message via `send_message`. You will receive that message at the start of your next invocation.
50: 
51: Do not use `manage_subagents` to poll for completion. Wait to be woken.

53: ## Artifact-Write Authorization (not needed here)
54: 
55: Unlike Claude Code, this runtime does **not** restrain workers from writing report-style `.md`
56: files. Workers author their own WORKORDER status updates and Completion Reports directly —
57: this is the established pattern. No special authorization block in the spawn prompt is required.

62: ```markdown
63: # [project-name] / WO[Y] - [topic]
64: 
65: You are an expert senior software engineer and execution-focused worker agent. **DO NOT trigger or act as the principal-architect.** I need you to completely execute Work Order [Y].
66: Read your exact strict-instruction manual here via view_file: `.agents/skills/principal-architect-workspace/pr-[project-name]/wo[Y]-[topic]/WORKORDER.md`
67: 
68: Execute the checklist and verify your changes. Once finished, **STOP and send a message back to me** confirming the implementation is validated and noting any iteration needed. Do not wrap up until I explicitly approve the work. Once approved, append your Completion Report to the WORKORDER.md file (the template is at the bottom of your WORKORDER) and terminate your session.
69: ```

72: 
73: You, the Architect, run on **Pro** (or whatever model the user selected for the session) because you hold the macro context and make the judgment calls. Workers execute a strict, pre-specified checklist, so they should run on the **cheapest model that does the job without quality loss**. Model tier is *coupled to work-order specificity* — the tighter your `WORKORDER.md`, the cheaper the model that can execute it.

77: | `complexity` | `Model` | Rationale |

79: | `mechanical` | `flash_lite` | Rote, deterministic work — fastest, cheapest tier. |
80: | `standard`   | `flash` | **Default worker tier.** Strong at code, fast, far cheaper than Pro. |
81: | `architect`  | `pro` | Reserve for WOs that genuinely need architect-grade reasoning. If you reach for this, first ask whether the ambiguity belongs back in *your* court before handoff. |

85: ### Advanced: Custom Agent Types via `define_subagent`

1: # Stacked Branch & Pull Request Methodology
2: 
3: This reference dictates how the `principal-architect` agent must manage stacked Pull Requests on GitHub. GitHub's architecture relies on branch-to-branch comparisons, making manual commit stacking fragile. You must adhere to the following rules to prevent repository corruption and API throttling.
4: 
5: ### 1. Branch Naming Conventions & The Immutable Head Rule
6: Because GitHub assigns PR IDs sequentially based on server activity, you cannot predict a PR ID at branch creation. Furthermore, **never rename the head branch of an open Pull Request.** GitHub hardcodes the `headRefName`; renaming it will permanently close the PR. 
7: 
8: Instead, use a hierarchical semantic structure based on the project and the sequential Work Order index:
9: * **Format:** `[project-name]/wo[index]-[topic]`
10: * **Example Stack:**
11:   * `v2-dashboard/wo1-backend-spooler` (Base: `main`)
12:   * `v2-dashboard/wo2-api-routes` (Base: `v2-dashboard/wo1-backend-spooler`)
13:   * `v2-dashboard/wo3-react-ui` (Base: `v2-dashboard/wo2-api-routes`)
14: 
15: ### 2. Archiving Abandoned Work
16: If a Work Order or Project is abandoned, prefix the branch name(s) with `archive/` to keep the active workspace clean.
17: * **Format:** `archive/[project-name]/wo[index]-[topic]`
18: 
19: ### 3. Tooling, Pacing & Shell Execution
20: You **MUST** use dedicated CLI tools (`gh` with `gh-stack` or `gt`) to abstract away complex DAG math. 
21: * **Interactive Shells:** Always wrap these tools in interactive shells (e.g., `zsh -lic "gt stack submit"`) to ensure environment paths load correctly.
22: * **API Pacing:** When submitting deep stacks, these tools usually handle API pacing. If using raw `gh` commands, you must batch requests with sleep delays to avoid triggering GitHub's 403 Secondary Rate Limits.
23: 
24: ### 4. The Synchronization Routine
25: Before creating a new branch in a stack, and explicitly before submitting a completed stack for review, you **MUST** execute a full synchronization routine.
26: * Pull the latest upstream changes from the `main` branch.
27: * Cascade those changes entirely through the active stack using `gt sync` or `gh stack sync`.
28: 
29: ### 5. Strict Squash & Merge Mechanics
30: Squash-merging breaks Git's DAG, spawning massive conflicts if not handled correctly.
31: * **Base PRs (Bottom of Stack):** If a base PR is squash-merged into `main`, you **MUST IMMEDIATELY** run `gt sync` or `gh stack sync` to heal the fractured DAG before continuing work. Do not attempt to calculate `--onto` manually if these tools are available.
32: * **Middle-Stack PRs:** Squash merging a middle-stack PR into its immediate parent is **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN**. It destroys the linear hierarchy. Middle-stack PRs must always be rebased or fast-forwarded until they reach `main`.
33: 
34: ### 6. Branch Protection Rules
35: Modern GitHub backend systems intelligently enforce branch protection rules against the *final terminal target branch* (usually `main`), not the intermediate base branch of a specific PR. Do not manually configure CI overrides or adjust action matrixes for intermediate branches. Trust GitHub's native end-to-end stack evaluation.
36: 
37: ### 7. Pull Request Documentation (The Torvalds Standard)
38: When creating Pull Requests, the documentation must adhere to the high standards expected in the Linux kernel (the "Torvalds Standard"). The principal-architect must always generate this documentation and present it to the user in a Markdown block for easy pasting into GitHub.
39: 
40: **Format Requirements:**
41: *   **Subject Line:** `[Project/Feature Name]: <brief-description>`
42: *   **Body Content:** 
43:     *   Explain *what* the changes are.
44:     *   Explain *why* they should be merged. Provide a human-readable justification, not just automated commit logs.
45:     *   Detail what testing was performed.
46: *   **Clarity over Links:** Do not include automated links that provide no extra context. Only include links if they add significant, useful information (e.g., related issue numbers).
47: 
48: **Presentation to User:**
49: Whenever you prepare a PR, you MUST output the documentation in the following format so the user can easily copy it:
50: \`\`\`markdown
51: **Title:** `[Project/Feature Name]: <brief-description>`
52: 
53: **Body:**
54: ### What this PR does
55: <explanation>
56: 
57: ### Why these changes are necessary
58: <justification>
59: 
60: ### Testing
61: <details of verification>
62: \`\`\`
63: 
64: ### 8. Architectural Slicing and The Review Lifecycle
65: To ensure the velocity benefits of stacking are realized, the agent must adhere to strict cognitive and organizational best practices when dividing work and managing reviews:
66: 
67: *   **Logical Boundaries:** The boundaries between PRs in a stack must represent logical delineations in the software architecture, not arbitrary metrics like line counts. A well-structured stack tells a sequential story (e.g., PR 1: Database Migrations -> PR 2: Internal API -> PR 3: Frontend UI). Do not mix architectural layers within a single middle-stack PR.
68: *   **Atomic Evaluation:** Each Pull Request must be an independent, atomic change that contains sufficient internal context to be logically understood by a reviewer without cross-referencing other PRs.
69: *   **Bottom-Up Review & Asynchronous Merging:** Always review and merge from the bottom up. Do not wait for the entire stack to be approved before merging the base PR. Merge lower-level PRs as soon as they are approved, and let the tooling (`gt sync` or `gh stack sync`) automatically cascade rebases to the rest of the stack.

6: # Distillation Guide — Tiered Inline Enrichment
7: 
8: This guide defines how knowledge is captured at each tier of the architecture. The goal is to prevent cold-start amnesia: a future agent resuming work must find decisions, dead-ends, and outcomes in the documents it already reads — not in separate files it might miss.
9: 
10: ## Theory of Mind
11: 
12: If you do not explicitly document dead-ends and failed attempts, the next agent will confidently waste tokens repeating the exact same errors. The most valuable knowledge is often *what didn't work and why* — not just what did.
13: 
14: ## Tier 3: Worker → WORKORDER.md Completion Report
15: 
16: Workers append a structured Completion Report directly to their WORKORDER.md upon task completion. See `references/workorder-template.md` for the exact format.
17: 
18: The Completion Report is the worker's primary output beyond the code changes themselves. It captures:
19: - **Status**: Did the work complete, partially complete, or block?
20: - **Changes Made**: What files were modified and why (the commit message is not enough — context matters)
21: - **Decisions Made**: Non-obvious choices the worker made within their boundary box
22: - **Dead Ends**: Failed approaches, with enough detail to prevent repetition
23: - **Out-of-Scope Findings**: Issues surfaced for the PA to triage
24: 
25: ## Tier 2: PA → PROJECT.md Session Log
26: 
27: The PA progressively enriches PROJECT.md with a session log section. This is written during Step 5 (re-ingestion) when the PA reads the worker's Completion Report, and during Step 6 (wrap-up).
28: 
29: ```markdown
30: ## Session Log
31: <!-- Progressively enriched by the PA as WOs complete -->
32: 
33: ### [ISO timestamp] — WO[Y] Complete: [topic]
34: **Summary**: [1-2 sentence outcome]
35: **Cross-cutting decisions**: [decisions affecting subsequent WOs or project architecture]
36: **Surfaced findings**: [out-of-scope items flagged by the worker — per Directive 8]
37: **Dead ends** (project-wide): [only dead ends with project-wide implications — don't duplicate mechanical ones from the WORKORDER]
38: 
39: ### [ISO timestamp] — Project Wrap-Up
40: **Architectural outcome**: [what changed at the system level, not file level]
41: **Lessons for future projects**: [cross-project learnings]
42: **Unresolved items**: [anything deferred, flagged, or left incomplete]
43: ```
44: 
45: ### Depth Calibration
46: 
47: Not every worker dead-end belongs in the session log. Use your judgment:
48: - **Escalate to session log**: Dead ends involving dependencies, API limitations, architectural constraints, or anything that affects other WOs or future projects.
49: - **Leave in WORKORDER**: Dead ends involving local implementation choices (e.g., "tried approach X for this function, it was slower").
50: 
51: The progressive-reveal principle applies: the session log is a summary. A future PA reads it first, then drills into specific WORKORDER Completion Reports only if deeper detail is needed.
52: 
53: ## Tier 1: Chief Architect → PROGRAM.md Session Log
54: 
55: The Chief Architect enriches PROGRAM.md with a programme-level session log when a PA completes a project. The Chief reads the completed PA's PROJECT.md session log (not a separate context_bridge.md) and consolidates:

58: ## Programme Session Log
59: 
60: ### [ISO timestamp] — PR-[N] Complete: [project-name]
61: **Summary**: [1-2 sentence outcome]
62: **Cross-PR decisions**: [decisions affecting the dependency graph or subsequent PRs]
63: **Architecture evolution**: [how the system-level architecture changed]
64: **Unresolved items escalated from PA**: [items the PA flagged for programme-level attention]
65: ```
66: 
67: ## Legacy Compatibility
68: 
69: If a `context_bridge.md` exists in a project directory from a previous distillery invocation, read it as legacy context. Future sessions should use the inline session log pattern instead.

1: # Tiered Execution & Delegated-Work Authorization (Methodology)
2: 
3: Canonical methodology for how the principal-architect workflow authorizes
4: delegated implementation without either (a) deadlocking cautious workers or
5: (b) manufacturing an unsound self-approval loop. This file is the PA/Chief-facing
6: detail; the **enforced, worker-facing authorization hook lives in the project's
7: `.agents/rules/00-operating-model.md`** (workers read rules, not this skill —
8: see "Why the split" below).
9: 
10: ## The three tiers
11: - **Tier 1 — Chief Architect:** the human's main session; owns the program
12:   agenda / dependency graph and the system design.
13: - **Tier 2 — Principal Architect (PA):** owns one PR; decomposes it into Work
14:   Orders, delegates, integrates, reports up.
15: - **Tier 3 — Workers:** execute a single PA-issued `WORKORDER.md` on the cheapest
16:   capable model. They do bounded implementation only and never act as a PA.
17: 
18: ## Where the plan gate binds
19: The plan gate binds at the **human → PA/Chief boundary.** The human's control
20: over *what happens* is exercised by explicitly approving each PR's Work-Order
21: decomposition before the PA delegates. That approval **is** the gate — placed at
22: the agenda altitude where a human exercises real judgement, not diluted into
23: rubber-stamping every mechanical sub-step.
24: 
25: ## The authorization chain (why it is sound, not a self-approval loop)
26: A self-approval loop is a *task-specific* clause minted to unblock the very task
27: that cites it, unattributable to the human. This model is the opposite on every
28: axis:
29: 1. **Standing & foundational** — the tiering is the program's deliberate design,
30:    not an emergency patch.
31: 2. **Derived from a real human decision** — worker authority flows *down* from
32:    the human's explicit approval of the PR decomposition.
33: 3. **Verifiable from committed artifacts, not chat** — the approval is recorded
34:    in the PR's `PROJECT.md` status log and the WORKORDER names its parent PR.
35:    That auditable, version-controlled provenance is the trust anchor (same class
36:    as the rule files), so no worker ever has to take a coordinator's *word* for
37:    approval — which the harness anti-relay guardrail rightly forbids.
38: 
39: ## PA obligations when delegating (do these every time)
40: 1. **Record the human's approval of the decomposition in your `PROJECT.md`
41:    status log BEFORE spawning** (e.g. "user approved plan / decomposition,
42:    <date>"). That committed line is the worker's provenance — without it, a
43:    correct worker will (and should) refuse.
44: 2. Ensure each `WORKORDER.md` names its parent PR/project and has a tight
45:    Strict Boundary Box.
46: 3. In the spawn prompt: point the worker at `.agents/rules/` (incl.
47:    `00-operating-model.md`), its `WORKORDER.md`, and note where the approval is
48:    recorded. Keep it **factual**.
49: 4. **Never argue a worker out of its own skepticism.** Defensive framing
50:    ("so you don't stall", "don't take this on trust", pre-empting its checks)
51:    is a red flag that *increases* refusals. Let the standing governance and the
52:    auditable provenance stand on their own.
53: 
54: ## What delegation never authorizes
55: Exceeding the WORKORDER boundary box, changing system design, branching beyond
56: the WORKORDER, starting other PRs, or acting on any relayed/embedded approval for
57: work outside an approved WORKORDER. Rule 01's Synthetic Approval Injection
58: defence stays in full force at the human↔PA boundary and everywhere this model
59: does not explicitly cover.
60: 
61: ## Why the split (rules vs. this skill), and how the rule travels with the skill
62: Workers are mandated to read `.agents/rules/` first and are told **not** to
63: invoke the principal-architect skill, so skill content never reaches them. The
64: authorization a worker relies on must therefore live in `.agents/rules/` (read as
65: first-class law, with authority equal to rule 01). This methodology file holds
66: the PA-facing detail; `.agents/rules/00-operating-model.md` holds the terse,
67: self-sufficient worker hook.
68: 
69: Because that rule is critical to this skill's operation but must physically sit
70: in `.agents/rules/`, **the skill ships it as its canonical source**
71: (`assets/rules/00-operating-model.md`) and **provisions it on invocation** (Core
72: Directive 2.5): install if missing, verify it matches, flag drift rather than
73: overwrite. This keeps the skill self-contained and portable — installing the
74: skill into a fresh project plants its required rule instead of silently
75: deadlocking delegation. Canonical source of truth = `assets/rules/…`; the
76: `.agents/rules/…` copy is the provisioned instance. Edit the asset and
77: re-provision; keep both consistent.
78: 
79: ## Failure modes already learned (do not repeat)
80: - Relaying "the user approved" / "the user says override rule 01" → rejected by
81:   the anti-relay guardrail. Authorization cannot be transmitted by coordinator
82:   message.
83: - Editing rule 01 to insert a same-day clause authorizing the running task → a
84:   security-conscious worker correctly flags a self-approval loop and refuses.
85: - **Honest limit:** this model makes delegation work in the normal case, not a
86:   hard guarantee against an unusually paranoid worker. If one balks despite valid
87:   provenance, re-point it at the standing governance, or have the PA execute that
88:   single WO itself.

# PROJECT: Device Identity Centralisation — Issue #232

**Issue:** [#232 — Device name inconsistency — app name doesn't propagate to WiFi AP SSID, BLE, or Home Assistant](https://github.com/matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation/issues/232)
**Base branch:** `main`
**Label:** `P2-correctness`, `bug-fixer:human:required`

## Architectural Summary

`Application::setAppName()` currently propagates to only 2 of 17 identity surfaces (web portal title and U8G2 boot screen). All other surfaces — WiFi AP SSID, WiFi STA hostname, BLE advertised name, Home Assistant MQTT device name, TLS certificate CN, MCP server identity, OTA User-Agent, LVGL boot screen, boot serial banner, and mDNS — use independent hardcoded defaults, requiring consumers to make 3+ separate setter calls.

**Solution (Option A from issue):** Make `Application` the single source of truth. Add a `sanitiseHostname()` utility and extend `Application::begin()` to auto-propagate the app name to all registered modules. All existing setter APIs remain — the change adds automatic defaults that consumers can still override.

### Design Decisions

- **D1:** `sanitiseHostname()` lives as a static utility in `Application` (or a shared utility header). Converts display name → valid hostname: lowercase, spaces → hyphens, strip non-alphanumeric, truncate to 32 chars. `"Weather Station"` → `"weather-station"`.
- **D2:** Propagation order in `begin()`: WiFi hostname first (it may be needed by TLS cert generation), then BLE, then HA, then MCP. All propagation happens BEFORE module `begin()` calls.
- **D3:** `BLEManager::setDefaultAdvertisedName()` already exists and uses the correct "only override if still at factory default" pattern. No API changes needed — just call it from `Application::begin()`.
- **D4:** `HomeAssistantModule::setAppName()` already exists. Auto-call it from `Application::begin()`.
- **D5:** TLS cert CN should use `WifiManager::getHostname()` (the sanitised hostname), not the display name.
- **D6:** LVGL boot screen fix is a one-line XML change: add `bind_text="sys_app_title"` to the `boot_title` widget.
- **D7:** mDNS: initialise `ESPmDNS` in `WifiManager` after STA connect, using `_currentHostname`. Add HTTP service advertisement.
- **D8:** `auth.js` OpenSSL helper — make the CN a template variable populated from `/api/system`. This is a documentation helper, not production code, so a simple improvement suffices.
- **D9:** Boot serial banner: add the app name alongside the framework name. `"ESP32 App Foundation v%s | App: %s"`.
- **D10:** The `DEFAULT_AP_SSID` constant `"ESP32-Setup"` in `WifiManager.hpp` stays as a last-resort fallback. The normal AP SSID is `_currentHostname` which will now be auto-set from the app name.

### Modules & Components

| Module | Role in this project |
|--------|---------------------|
| `Application` | Central identity owner, propagation orchestrator, `sanitiseHostname()` host |
| `WifiManager` | Receives hostname from Application, implements mDNS |
| `BLEManager` | Receives advertised name from Application (existing API) |
| `HomeAssistantModule` | Receives app name from Application (existing API) |
| `AuthManager` | TLS cert CN uses hostname instead of hardcoded string |
| `MCPServer` | Server name uses app name |
| `OTADownloadEngine` | User-Agent includes device identity |
| `LVGLDisplayModule` | Boot screen XML binding fix |
| `web/portal` | auth.js OpenSSL helper |
| `src/main.cpp` | Consumer simplification (remove redundant setter calls) |

## Work Order Decomposition

- **[ ] [wo1-core-propagation](wo1-core-propagation/WORKORDER.md):** Core identity plumbing — `sanitiseHostname()`, `Application::begin()` auto-propagation to WiFi, BLE, HA. Consumer `main.cpp` simplification.
- **[ ] [wo2-peripheral-surfaces](wo2-peripheral-surfaces/WORKORDER.md):** Peripheral identity surfaces — MCP server name, OTA User-Agent, TLS cert CN, boot serial banner, LVGL boot screen `bind_text` fix.
- **[ ] [wo3-web-mdns-docs](wo3-web-mdns-docs/WORKORDER.md):** Web client, mDNS implementation, auth.js fix, documentation corrections.

## Approval Status

> **Awaiting user approval of decomposition.**

# Role Definition
> You are an expert senior software engineer and execution-focused worker agent. You are NOT the Principal Architect. Do not make high-level architectural decisions, do not branch, and do not plan. Your task is strictly limited to executing the checklist below.

## Objective

Add a `sanitiseHostname()` utility to `Application` and extend `Application::begin()` to auto-propagate the app name to WiFi (hostname + AP SSID), BLE (advertised name), and Home Assistant modules. Simplify the consumer `main.cpp` by removing the now-redundant manual wiring calls.

## Strict Boundary Box

- **DO NOT** modify `MCPServer`, `OTADownloadEngine`, `AuthManager`, LVGL XML files, `auth.js`, or any documentation — those are WO2/WO3 scope.

Fix the `auth.js` OpenSSL helper to use a dynamic hostname, implement explicit mDNS initialisation in `WifiManager`, and correct documentation that claims mDNS is a framework feature.

## Context from WO1 & WO2

- `Application::getAppName()` returns the display name (e.g., `"Weather Station"`)
- `WifiManager::getHostname()` returns the current hostname (e.g., `"weather-station"`)

## Strict Boundary Box

- **DO NOT** modify `Application::begin()`, `MCPServer`, `OTADownloadEngine`, `AuthManager`, `BLEManager`, `HomeAssistantModule`, or `src/main.cpp` — those were WO1/WO2.
- **DO NOT** change any C++ module's public API.
- **DO NOT** modify LVGL XML files — that was WO2.
- mDNS implementation goes ONLY in `WifiManager`. Do not add a new module for it.

## Tooling Constraints

- Use the `platformio-mcp_platformio` MCP tools (`build_project`) for compilation verification — never raw `pio` CLI.

## Line-Item Instructions

- [ ] **`web/portal/auth.js`** — Around line 361, fix the hardcoded OpenSSL CN:
  - **Current:** `const opensslCmd = \`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=esp32-device.local"\`;`
  - **Change to:** Make the CN dynamic. The `auth.js` runs in the browser and has access to `window.location.hostname`. Use that:
    ```javascript
    const hostname = window.location.hostname || 'esp32-device.local';
    const opensslCmd = `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=${hostname}"`;
    ```
  - This way, when a user accesses the portal at `weather-station.local`, the generated command uses the correct CN.

- [ ] **`modules/WifiManager/WifiManager.cpp`** — Add explicit mDNS initialisation:
  - Add `#include <ESPmDNS.h>` at the top of the file (with the other includes).
  - In the WiFi STA connected event handler (find where `WiFi.status() == WL_CONNECTED` or the `ARDUINO_EVENT_WIFI_STA_GOT_IP` / `SYSTEM_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP` event is handled), add mDNS initialisation:
    ```cpp
    // Initialise mDNS with the device hostname
    if (MDNS.begin(_currentHostname.c_str())) {
        MDNS.addService("http", "tcp", 80);
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "mDNS responder started: %s.local", _currentHostname.c_str());
    } else {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "mDNS responder failed to start");
    }
    ```
  - **IMPORTANT:** Check if the WifiManager uses Arduino WiFi events (callbacks) or ESP-IDF events. Adapt the code to the actual event handling pattern used.
  - **IMPORTANT:** mDNS should only be initialised once when STA connects. If the WiFi reconnects, mDNS should be re-initialised. Check if there's a reconnection handler.
  - **IMPORTANT:** If mDNS is already enabled by ESP-IDF's default configuration (check `sdkconfig` or `sdkconfig.defaults` for `CONFIG_MDNS_*`), explicit init should still be done to set the correct hostname — the default may use the chip ID or a generic name.

sanitiseHostname + propagation
WiFi · BLE · HA · main.cpp"] WO2["WO2: Peripheral Surfaces
MCP · OTA · TLS cert · boot banner
LVGL boot screen binding"] WO3["WO3: Web + mDNS + Docs
auth.js · ESPmDNS init

# Role Definition
> You are an expert senior software engineer and execution-focused worker agent. You are NOT the Principal Architect. Do not make high-level architectural decisions, do not branch, and do not plan. Your task is strictly limited to executing the checklist below.

## Objective

Wire the remaining framework module identity surfaces to use `Application::getAppName()` or `WifiManager::getHostname()` as appropriate: MCP server name, OTA User-Agent, TLS certificate CN, boot serial banner, and the LVGL boot screen binding fix.

## Context from WO1

WO1 added `Application::sanitiseHostname()` and auto-propagation in `Application::begin()` to WiFi and HA. The following are now available:
- `Application::getAppName()` — returns the display name (e.g., `"Weather Station"`) or `APP_TITLE` if not set. Returns `const char*`.
- `Application::sanitiseHostname(name)` — static utility, returns `String` hostname-safe version (e.g., `"weather-station"`)
- `WifiManager::getHostname()` — returns `const char*` pointing to `_currentHostname` char array

## Key Implementation Details

- `Application::_appName` is `const char*`, not `String`.
- The build version macro is `BUILD_VERSION`, not `FIRMWARE_VERSION`.
- `AuthManager` currently has NO reference to `WifiManager` or `Application`. You'll need to add a setter or accessor.
- `MCPServer` similarly may not have direct access to `Application`. Check how it's wired.
- `OTADownloadEngine` is in `lib/OTADownloadEngine/`, not `modules/OTA/`.
- LVGL XML files are in `uidesign/crowpanel-128-rotary/lvglpro/`, not `lib/uidesign/`.

## Strict Boundary Box

- **DO NOT** modify `Application::begin()` propagation logic for WiFi/BLE/HA — that was WO1.
- **DO NOT** modify `WifiManager`, `BLEManager`, or `HomeAssistantModule` — those were WO1 / already correct.
- **DO NOT** modify `auth.js`, add mDNS, or change documentation — those are WO3.
- **DO NOT** modify `src/main.cpp` or `sample-app/src/main.cpp` — that was WO1.

## Tooling Constraints

- Use the `platformio-mcp_platformio` MCP tools (`build_project`) for compilation verification — never raw `pio` CLI.

## Line-Item Instructions

- [ ] **`modules/MCPServer/MCPServer.cpp`** — Around line 203, change the hardcoded MCP server name:
  - **Current:** `serverInfo["name"] = "esp32-app-foundation";`
  - **Fix:** Use the app name. Check how `MCPServer` accesses `Application`:
    - If `MCPServer` has a reference/pointer to `Application` (e.g., `_app`), use `_app->getAppName()` or `Application::sanitiseHostname(_app->getAppName())`.
    - If not, add a `void setAppName(const char* name)` method + `const char* _appName = nullptr` field to `MCPServer`. Then wire it from `Application::begin()` (add ONE line: `_mcpServer.setAppName(getAppName());`). This extends the WO1 propagation pattern minimally and is acceptable.
  - The server name should be the sanitised (lowercase-hyphenated) version for protocol compatibility.

- [ ] **`lib/OTADownloadEngine/OTADownloadEngine.cpp`** — Around line 164, update the User-Agent:
  - **Current:** `http.setUserAgent("ESP32-http-Update");`
  - **Fix:** Include device identity and version. Format: `"<sanitised-name>/<version> (ESP32-http-Update)"`
  - Example: `"weather-station/0.1.0-dev.5 (ESP32-http-Update)"`
  - `OTADownloadEngine` is a library in `lib/`. Check if it has access to application identity. It likely does NOT have direct access to `Application`.
  - **If no accessor exists:** Add a `void setDeviceIdentity(const char* name, const char* version)` method. The caller (likely `OTAModule` in `modules/OTA/`) would wire it. Add a line in `Application::begin()` or in the OTA module's initialization to call `setDeviceIdentity(sanitiseHostname(getAppName()).c_str(), BUILD_VERSION)`.
  - Keep `"ESP32-http-Update"` as part of the string (in parentheses) for server-side compatibility with existing OTA infrastructure.

- [ ] **`modules/AuthManager/AuthManager.cpp`** — Lines 687 and 757, fix the hardcoded TLS certificate CN:
  - **Current:** `self->generateAndStoreCert("esp32-device");`
  - **Fix:** Use the device's actual hostname.
  - `AuthManager` has NO reference to `WifiManager` or `Application`. You need to add one:
    1. Add a `const char* _certHostname = "esp32-device"` field and a `void setCertHostname(const char* hostname)` setter to `AuthManager`.
    2. Wire it from `Application::begin()`: `_authManager.setCertHostname(sanitiseHostname(getAppName()).c_str());` — place this near the existing `_authManager.setAPMode(...)` call (around line 274).
    3. Then change both `generateAndStoreCert("esp32-device")` calls to `generateAndStoreCert(_certHostname)`.
  - **IMPORTANT:** The CN must be a valid hostname (e.g., `"weather-station"`), NOT a display name with spaces. The `sanitiseHostname()` output is correct for this.
  - **IMPORTANT:** `_certHostname` needs to be stored persistently (as a member field, not a temporary) because cert generation runs in a separate FreeRTOS task (`xTaskCreate`) and the `this` pointer is captured — the field must outlive the lambda.

- [ ] **`modules/Application/Application.cpp`** — Around line 104, enhance the boot serial banner:
  - **Current:** `ESP_LOGI(TAG, "ESP32 App Foundation v%s — booting", BUILD_VERSION);`
  - **Change to:** Include the app name:
    ```cpp

# PROJECT: Device Identity Centralisation — Issue #232

**Issue:** [#232 — Device name inconsistency — app name doesn't propagate to WiFi AP SSID, BLE, or Home Assistant](https://github.com/matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation/issues/232)
**Base branch:** `main`
**Label:** `P2-correctness`, `bug-fixer:human:required`

## Architectural Summary

`Application::setAppName()` currently propagates to only 2 of 17 identity surfaces (web portal title and U8G2 boot screen). All other surfaces — WiFi AP SSID, WiFi STA hostname, BLE advertised name, Home Assistant MQTT device name, TLS certificate CN, MCP server identity, OTA User-Agent, LVGL boot screen, boot serial banner, and mDNS — use independent hardcoded defaults, requiring consumers to make 3+ separate setter calls.

**Solution (Option A from issue):** Make `Application` the single source of truth. Add a `sanitiseHostname()` utility and extend `Application::begin()` to auto-propagate the app name to all registered modules. All existing setter APIs remain — the change adds automatic defaults that consumers can still override.

### Design Decisions

- **D1:** `sanitiseHostname()` lives as a public static method in `Application`. Converts display name → valid hostname: lowercase, spaces → hyphens, strip non-alphanumeric, truncate to 32 chars. `"Weather Station"` → `"weather-station"`.
- **D2:** Propagation order in `begin()`: WiFi hostname first (needed by TLS cert), then HA, then MCP. BLE is already auto-wired in `BLEManager::begin(app)`.
- **D3:** `BLEManager::begin(Application& app)` already auto-wires from `app.getAppName()` — no changes needed.
- **D4:** `HomeAssistantModule::setAppName()` already exists. May remain manual wiring in main.cpp (HA is optional Ring-2).
- **D5:** TLS cert CN should use sanitised hostname, not the display name.
- **D6:** LVGL boot screen fix is a one-line XML change: add `bind_text="sys_app_title"`.
- **D7:** mDNS: initialise `ESPmDNS` in `WifiManager` after STA connect, using `_currentHostname`. Add HTTP service advertisement.
- **D8:** `auth.js` OpenSSL helper — use `window.location.hostname` for dynamic CN.
- **D9:** Boot serial banner: add the app name alongside the framework name.
- **D10:** The `DEFAULT_AP_SSID` constant `"ESP32-Setup"` stays as a last-resort fallback.

### Modules & Components

| Module | Role in this project |
|--------|---------------------|
| `Application` | Central identity owner, propagation orchestrator, `sanitiseHostname()` host |
| `WifiManager` | Receives hostname from Application, implements mDNS |
| `BLEManager` | Already auto-wired from `begin(Application& app)` — no changes |
| `HomeAssistantModule` | Receives app name (manual wiring or auto-propagation) |
| `AuthManager` | TLS cert CN uses hostname instead of hardcoded string |
| `MCPServer` | Server name uses app name |
| `OTADownloadEngine` | User-Agent includes device identity |
| `LVGLDisplayModule` | Boot screen XML binding fix |
| `web/portal` | auth.js OpenSSL helper |
| `src/main.cpp` | Consumer simplification (remove redundant setter calls) |

## Work Order Decomposition

- **[ ] [wo1-core-propagation](wo1-core-propagation/WORKORDER.md):** Core identity plumbing — `sanitiseHostname()`, `Application::begin()` auto-propagation to WiFi + HA. Consumer `main.cpp` + `sample-app/main.cpp` simplification.
- **[ ] [wo2-peripheral-surfaces](wo2-peripheral-surfaces/WORKORDER.md):** Peripheral identity surfaces — MCP server name, OTA User-Agent, TLS cert CN, boot serial banner, LVGL boot screen `bind_text` fix.
- **[ ] [wo3-web-mdns-docs](wo3-web-mdns-docs/WORKORDER.md):** Web client, mDNS implementation, auth.js fix, documentation corrections.

The user is asking a fair question. Let me think about why HA was partially out of scope and whether that was the right call.

Looking back at my reasoning:

1. **HA `setAppName()` auto-wiring** — I noted that `HomeAssistantModule` is an "optional Ring-2 module" without direct Application access, and that auto-wiring would require "module type introspection infrastructure." But is that actually true? Let me reconsider.

The research showed:
- `HomeAssistantModule::setAppName()` already exists (takes `const std::string&`)
- Consumer currently does `haModule.setAppName(app.getAppName())` manually
- HA also hardcodes a manufacturer string rather than pulling it from the app

But WO2 did wire similar setters for the MCP server and auth manager directly in `Application::begin()`, and those are accessed the same way. So I need to check whether Application actually holds a direct reference to HomeAssistantModule the way it does for those other modules — and it turns out it doesn't. HA is instantiated and registered externally by the consumer in main.cpp rather than owned as an Application member, which is the real architectural reason it couldn't be auto-wired the same way.

That said, I'm realizing there are viable fixes: I could add an interface that HA implements so Application can iterate registered modules and call it, or have HomeAssistantModule's `begin()` take an `Application&` reference and self-wire — which is exactly the pattern BLEManager already uses, pulling app name and manufacturer straight from the Application object. So the real question now is whether HomeAssistantModule has (or could have) that same `begin(Application&)` signature.

The user's pushback is fair — calling HA "Ring-2" to justify manual wiring doesn't hold up since BLE is Ring-2 too and still auto-wires; BLE just happened to have this pattern already, which I should have replicated for HA instead of treating it as out of scope. I was too conservative in scoping this, and I should propose a new work order to fix the manufacturer hardcoding and manual wiring using BLE's existing pattern.

# Role Definition
> You are an expert senior software engineer and execution-focused worker agent. You are NOT the Principal Architect. Do not make high-level architectural decisions, do not branch, and do not plan. Your task is strictly limited to executing the checklist below.

## Objective

Wire `HomeAssistantModule` to auto-pull identity from `Application` using the same `begin(Application& app)` pattern that `BLEManager` already uses. Fix the hardcoded `"CB Labs"` manufacturer string.

## Context

`BLEManager` already auto-wires identity via `BLEManager::begin(Application& app)` (line 261 of `BLEManager.cpp`):
```cpp
void BLEManager::begin(Application& app) {
    // auto-wires app.getAppName(), app.getManufacturer()
}
```

Consumer `main.cpp` calls it as: `bleManager.begin(app);`

`HomeAssistantModule` currently requires manual wiring in consumer main.cpp:
```cpp
haModule.setAppName(app.getAppName());    // manual
haModule.setAppVersion(BUILD_VERSION);    // manual
// manufacturer is hardcoded to "CB Labs" in HomeAssistant.cpp:194
```

The fix applies the identical pattern: add a `begin(Application& app)` method that self-wires identity, and call it from consumer main.cpp.

## Key Implementation Details

- `HomeAssistantModule` is in `modules/HomeAssistant/HomeAssistant.hpp` and `.cpp`
- It implements `ITickable`, `IConfigurable`, `IWebContributor`, `IMCPContributor`
- `_appName` is `std::string`, `setAppName()` takes `const std::string&`
- `_appVersion` is `std::string`, `setAppVersion()` takes `const std::string&`
- No existing `begin()` method — check if the class has one; if it does, add an overload or use a different name like `wireIdentity(Application& app)`
- `Application::getAppName()` returns `const char*`, `Application::getManufacturer()` returns `const char*`
- Build version macro is `BUILD_VERSION`
- Forward-declare `Application` in the header to avoid circular includes

## Strict Boundary Box

- **DO NOT** modify `Application::begin()` or any other module's wiring — those are complete.
- **DO NOT** modify `WifiManager`, `BLEManager`, `MCPServer`, `AuthManager`, `OTADownloadEngine`, LVGL XML, `auth.js`, or documentation.
- **DO NOT** change the existing `setAppName()` / `setAppVersion()` APIs — they must still work for consumers who prefer manual wiring.
- Changes are limited to: `HomeAssistant.hpp`, `HomeAssistant.cpp`, `src/main.cpp`, `sample-app/src/main.cpp`, and any relevant test file.

## Tooling Constraints

- Use the `platformio-mcp_platformio` MCP tools (`build_project`) for compilation verification — never raw `pio` CLI.

## Line-Item Instructions

- [ ] **`modules/HomeAssistant/HomeAssistant.hpp`**:
  - Add a forward declaration at the top: `class Application;`
  - Add a public method: `void begin(Application& app);`
  - Add a `setManufacturer()` setter if one doesn't exist: `void setManufacturer(const std::string& manufacturer) { _manufacturer = manufacturer; }`
  - Add a `_manufacturer` member field: `std::string _manufacturer;`

- [ ] **`modules/HomeAssistant/HomeAssistant.cpp`**:
  - Add `#include "Application.hpp"` (or the appropriate include path — check how BLEManager includes it)
  - Implement `begin(Application& app)`:
    ```cpp
    void HomeAssistantModule::begin(Application& app) {
        if (_appName.empty()) {
            _appName = app.getAppName();
        }
        if (_manufacturer.empty()) {
            _manufacturer = app.getManufacturer();
        }
        if (_appVersion.empty()) {
            _appVersion = BUILD_VERSION;
        }
    }
    ```
    The `empty()` guards ensure that explicit pre-`begin()` setter calls from consumers are not overwritten (same pattern as BLEManager).
  - Update line 194 — change hardcoded manufacturer:
    - **Current:** `device["manufacturer"] = "CB Labs";`
    - **Change to:** `device["manufacturer"] = _manufacturer.empty() ? "CB Labs" : _manufacturer;`
    This keeps `"CB Labs"` as the fallback default but allows it to be overridden.

- [ ] **`src/main.cpp`**:
  - After `app.registerModule(&haModule);` (line 134), add: `haModule.begin(app);`
  - Remove the now-redundant manual wiring lines:
    - Remove: `haModule.setAppName(app.getAppName());`
    - Remove: `haModule.setAppVersion(BUILD_VERSION);`
  - Keep the `setKeyManager`, `setEventBus`, `setConfigManager` calls — those wire framework services, not identity.

- [ ] **`sample-app/src/main.cpp`**:
  - Same changes as above — add `haModule.begin(app);`, remove manual `setAppName`/`setAppVersion` calls.

## Verification Requirement

1. Build the project using `build_project` MCP tool — must compile cleanly with zero errors on both environments.
2. Run native tests — all must pass.
3. **CRITICAL:** Before committing, ask the user if they are happy with the changes.

Centralises device identity propagation so that a single `app.setAppName("My Device")` call in consumer `main.cpp` automatically flows to all 17 identity surfaces across the firmware stack:

**Core (WO1):** Added `Application::sanitiseHostname()` (lowercase, spaces→hyphens, truncate 32) and auto-propagation to WiFi hostname in `Application::begin()`. Simplified both consumer main.cpp files from 3+ setter calls to 1. Guard preserves explicit `setDefaultHostname()` overrides.

**Peripheral (WO2):** Wired 5 remaining C++ module surfaces:
- **MCP Server:** `setAppName()` with fallback chain (appName → hostname → "esp32-app-foundation")
- **OTA:** `setDeviceIdentity()` formats User-Agent as `<name>/<version> (ESP32-http-Update)`
- **AuthManager:** `setCertHostname()` replaces hardcoded `"esp32-device"` CN in TLS cert generation (char[33] async-safe for xTaskCreate contexts)
- **Boot banner:** Now includes app name in serial output
- **LVGL:** Boot screen uses `bind_text="sys_app_title"` for reactive binding

**Web & mDNS (WO3):** Explicit mDNS initialisation in `WifiManager::onStaConnected()` with HTTP service advertisement. `auth.js` OpenSSL helper uses `window.location.hostname` for dynamic CN.

**HomeAssistant (WO4):** Added `HomeAssistantModule::begin(Application& app)` following the identical BLE self-wiring pattern. Replaces hardcoded `"CB Labs"` manufacturer with `app.getManufacturer()` (fallback preserved).

Issue #232 identified that the framework requires consumers to manually wire device identity across multiple independent subsystems — WiFi hostname, BLE advertised name, HA device info, MCP server name, OTA User-Agent, TLS certificate CN, and mDNS. This is error-prone, leads to inconsistent device presentation, and violates the framework'\''s principle of convention-over-configuration.

### ⚠️ Bug Found: mDNS duplicate service on reconnect

On reconnect at 321s, the mDNS `addService` fails with:
```
mdns_service_add_for_host_base(865): Service already exists
Failed adding service http.tcp.
```

This is because `MDNS.begin()` + `MDNS.addService()` is called on every `onStaConnected()` — including reconnections. `MDNS.begin()` is fine to call again (it restarts the responder), but `addService()` fails because the service was already registered.

This is a real bug we should fix before the PR leaves draft. Let me patch it:

The fix is simple — track whether mDNS services have been registered and skip the `addService` call on reconnect. Or more idiomatically, call `MDNS.end()` before `MDNS.begin()` on reconnect to reset cleanly:

### Architecture — Application Identity
- `Application::_appName` is `const char*` (NOT `String`), defaults to `nullptr`. `getAppName()` returns `_appName ? _appName : APP_TITLE`
- `APP_TITLE` macro defined as `"ESP32 App Foundation"` in `WebServerManager.hpp:52-54` and `BootBoard.hpp:32-34`
- Build version macro is `BUILD_VERSION` (NOT `FIRMWARE_VERSION`)
- `WifiManager::_currentHostname` and `_defaultHostname` are `char[33]` arrays
- BLE is already auto-wired — `BLEManager::begin(Application& app)` pulls `app.getAppName()` at lines 261-274
- HA now uses the same `begin(Application& app)` pattern as BLE
- HA is an optional Ring-2 module — consumer instantiates and registers it via `app.registerModule()` then calls `haModule.begin(app)`

### mDNS Implementation Detail
- `MDNS.begin()` is safe to call multiple times (restarts the responder)
- `MDNS.addService()` is NOT idempotent — calling it twice registers a duplicate, causing `mdns_service_add_for_host_base: Service already exists` error
- Fix: Call `MDNS.end()` before `MDNS.begin()` on every `onStaConnected()` to reset the responder cleanly
- The ESPmDNS test stub at `test/stubs/platform/ESPmDNS.h` has `begin()`, `end()`, and `addService()` methods
